author: Michael Larabel
description: Dynamic PAMT has made it for Linux 7.4! Dynamic PAMT is a new feature for reducing memory overhead on Intel TDX servers where there may not be many concurrent virtual machines occupying a majority of the system. In today's world with high memory prices and tight availability, Dynamic PAMT provides nice memory overhead reduction for modern Intel Xeon servers...
title: Dynamic PAMT Merged For Linux 7.4 To Help Intel Servers Save Precious RAM

author: Michael Larabel
description: System76 developers just released COSMIC Epoch 1.11 as the newest point release to their Rust-written open-source desktop environment catering to their in-house Pop!_OS Linux distribution...
title: COSMIC Epoch 1.11 Released With Wayland xdg-dialog-v1, Better Multi-GPU Handling

author: Michael Larabel
description: Among the many VFS pull requests merged as the initial material for the in-development Linux 7.4, the VFS IOmap pull introduced lazy bounce buffering for checksummed reads. This improvement is benefiting checksumming on XFS with improved performance and lower resource usage...
title: Improved Performance & Resource Usage For XFS Checksumming With Linux 7.4

author: Michael Larabel
description: Intel has long worked on tuning their oneDNN neural network library for their hardware and saw its adoption by PyTorch and other AI frameworks. AMD has maintained ZenDNN as their downstream fork that is oneDNN API compatible while catering to their Zen processor designs. As an interesting twist, AMD and Intel jointly announced today they will be collaborating around oneDNN for PyTorch and pushing the AMD Zen improvements into oneDNN...
title: Intel & AMD Now Collaborating On Software Optimizations With PyTorch/oneDNN

author: Michael Larabel
description: For those running a Star Labs StarFighter Ultra or other Intel Core Ultra Arrow Lake laptop, the recent Ubuntu 26.10 release is providing some nice performance gains over the Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release. Here is a look at how Ubuntu 26.04 LTS vs. Ubuntu 26.10 performs with the Intel Core Ultra 9 285H over dozens of different benchmarks.
title: Intel Core Ultra 9 Arrow Lake On Star Labs StarFighter Shows Nice Gains On Ubuntu 26.10

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Linux Foundation published a new study today around the impact of generative AI on open-source software development. One key takeaway is that ~25% of new open-source software pull requests amount to AI slop...
title: Linux Foundation Estimates 25% Of New Pull Requests To Be Low-Quality AI Slop

author: Michael Larabel
description: Added to the Linux kernel last year was Coredump support via Unix domain sockets as an alternative to the pipe-based Coredumps. With code now merged for Linux 7.4, the core dumps via sockets has the potential of being much smaller thanks to sparse support. In extreme cases they can be 1% of the size without sparse support...
title: Linux Coredumps Via Sockets Can Be Much Smaller Now With Sparse Support

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linus Torvalds began honoring pull requests overnight of new code entering the Linux 7.4 kernel -- as well as removing old code. BFS is the latest obsolete file-system removed from the mainline kernel...
title: BFS Removed With Linux 7.4 As Old UnixWare File-System

author: Michael Larabel
description: Following last week's release of Plasma 6.8, the Plasma 6.8.1 point release is out today with dozens of bug fixes...
title: KDE Plasma 6.8.1 Released With Dozens Of Fixes

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Omarchy Linux distribution to date has been centered on x86_64 support for this Arch Linux distribution. Released today was Omarchy 4.5-RC1 and with this new version there is initial AArch64 support centered around Snapdragon X and NVIDIA N1X laptop support...
title: Omarchy 4.5 Expanding To AArch64 World With Snapdragon X & NVIDIA N1X Laptops

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linux 7.4 is seeing a new emulation function added for cmpxchg() for compare and exchange. This is being done so that two-byte cmpxchg() can be used in common Linux kernel code that is already natively supported on newer CPU architectures. The pull request notes though that some old CPU architectures might no longer be supported by the Linux kernel moving ahead...
title: Linux 7.4 Adding New Emulation Function While Some Old CPUs May Soon Be Phased Out

author: Michael Larabel
description: Miguel Ojeda sent out his pull request of the new Rust kernel code slated for introduction in Linux 7.4. It's a big one this round due to updating the Zerocopy vendored library plus updating other Rust crates for the kernel...
title: 17k Lines Of New Rust Kernel Code Heading Into Linux 7.4

author: Michael Larabel
description: Theo de Raadt released OpenBSD 8.0 today as the 61st release of this BSD operating system...
title: OpenBSD 8.0 Released With Intel Arc A-Series, Other Hardware Improvements
